HSTU (2024) already supports jointly learned positional and temporal attention biases alongside SiLU attention and multiplicative gating. Meta’s implementation learns separate position and bucketed time-gap parameters, providing a direct way to distinguish closely spaced interactions from older history within one HSTU backbone. Temporal bias need not enforce monotonic decay: older interactions can remain useful when predictive. [HSTU paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2402.17152), [official implementation](https://github.com/meta-recsys/generative-recommenders/blob/main/generative_recommenders/research/modeling/sequential/hstu.py).

Related work offers lightweight session mechanisms. A 2025 study proposes session tokens, session segment embeddings and temporal self-attention, reporting improvements with limited parameter overhead. Decoupled Temporal Encoding (2026) separates personalized macro-temporal features from local sequence order, applying relative-order bias when interactions are temporally dense. These suggest combining elapsed-time information with a learned distinction between local activity and broader history. [Session-aware recommendation](https://doi.org/10.1109/ACCESS.2025.3545243), [DTE](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.16274).

Research hypothesis for this benchmark: augment the single HSTU with log-bucketed observed time gaps and a jointly trained gate conditioned on adjacent gaps and history representations, allowing attention to older events to vary with current context. This is an adaptation hypothesis, not an established Amazon HR@10 gain. Treat session boundaries as uncertain temporal cues; purchases and inactivity do not establish satisfaction or fulfilled needs. Use only timestamps available at inference—never a held-out target’s timestamp unless the evaluator explicitly supplies it as query context.
